governingStatute: Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015 read with Section 133 of Companies Act, 2013 and US GAAP FASB Accounting Standards Codification Topic 842
statutorySection: Ind AS 116 (Leases) converged with IFRS 16 and aligned with US GAAP ASC 842
title: Lease Accounting & On-Balance-Sheet Capitalization (Right-of-Use Asset & Lease Liability Amortization)

effectivePeriod.annualReset: Continuous lease modification, remeasurement, and interest/depreciation split at reporting dates
effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: Mandatory standard notified via MCA G.S.R. 273(E) effective FY 2019-20 onwards.

plainTextSummary: Under Ind AS 116 (converged with IFRS 16 and aligned with US GAAP ASC 842), lessees must recognize a Right-of-Use (ROU) Asset and a corresponding Lease Liability for all leases on the balance sheet, eliminating the off-balance-sheet operating lease classification previously allowed under Ind AS 17. The only exceptions are short-term leases (term of 12 months or less with no purchase option) and leases of low-value assets (underlying asset value < approx. USD 5,000 / INR 4 Lakhs). At the lease commencement date, the Lease Liability is measured at the present value of future lease payments discounted using the interest rate implicit in the lease, or if that rate cannot be readily determined, the lessee's Incremental Borrowing Rate (IBR). The ROU Asset is measured initially at cost, comprising the initial lease liability, lease payments made at or prior to commencement date, initial direct costs, and estimated restoration/decommissioning costs, less lease incentives received. Subsequentially, the ROU Asset is depreciated straight-line over the lease term (or economic life if ownership transfers), while the Lease Liability is accreted using the effective interest method (recognizing interest expense in profit or loss) and reduced by cash lease payments. This results in a front-loaded total expense profile in P&L (higher interest in early years). For dual-reporting entities, reconciliation must bridge Ind AS 116 single-lessee model with US GAAP ASC 842 dual-model (which retains a single straight-line lease cost for operating leases) and Indian Income Tax Section 32/37 rent deduction schedules.

Incremental Borrowing Rate (IBR) methodology memorandum citing institutional lender quotes or yield curves

Deferred Tax (Ind AS 12 / ASC 740) workpaper calculating temporary timing difference between ROU expense and tax rent deduction
